questions.q: A material expands strongly when wetted and is used in liners and waterproofing systems because it is a clay. Which material is it?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - stone, tile and paving terminology
questions.n: Bentonite is an expansive clay used in geosynthetic clay liners and waterproofing applications; it is not a bituminous material.

questions.q: Why is asphalt pavement called flexible pavement?
o: It carries loads through rebar only
It is laid without any base
It spreads loads by bending, not slab action
questions.ref: Federal Highway Administration, pavement design and rehabilitation guidance
questions.n: Flexible pavement carries traffic loads through layered materials that deform and distribute stresses without rigid slab action.

questions.q: A cladding sample shows crystalline interlocking grains and comes from a rock formed by cooling magma. Which stone family best fits the description?
questions.ref: Natural Stone Institute, Dimension Stone Design Manual
questions.n: The magma-origin clue identifies an igneous rock; granite is the common dimension-stone choice among the options.

questions.q: A project needs a flexible vehicular pavement capable of conventional asphalt resurfacing later. Which surface system best matches that requirement?
questions.ref: Federal Highway Administration, pavement design and rehabilitation guidance
questions.n: Asphalt is the conventional flexible pavement system and can be rehabilitated by milling and asphalt overlays.

questions.q: An aging hot-mix asphalt parking area is to be rehabilitated by placing a new concrete slab directly over the asphalt. What is this treatment called?
questions.ref: American Concrete Pavement Association (ACPA), whitetopping and concrete-overlay guidance
questions.n: A concrete overlay on existing asphalt pavement is whitetopping.

questions.q: What water-absorption range is traditionally associated with vitreous ceramic tile?
questions.ref: ANSI A137.1 - American National Standard Specifications for Ceramic Tile
questions.n: Traditional ceramic-tile terminology classifies vitreous tile in the low-absorption range of more than 0.5% up to 3%.

questions.q: Which common dimension stone is metamorphic?
questions.ref: ASTM C503/C503M - Standard Specification for Marble Dimension Stone
questions.n: Marble forms by metamorphism of carbonate rock such as limestone or dolostone.

questions.q: What is the principal binder in modern asphalt pavement?
questions.ref: Asphalt Institute, The Asphalt Handbook / pavement materials terminology
questions.n: Modern hot-mix asphalt uses asphalt binder to coat and bind aggregate particles.

questions.q: A ceramic tile has a measured absorption of 2.0%. Which traditional absorption class does it fall into?
questions.ref: ANSI A137.1 - American National Standard Specifications for Ceramic Tile
questions.n: A 2.0% absorption lies within the traditional 0.5%–3.0% vitreous range.

questions.q: Which standard specifically covers granite dimension stone?
questions.ref: ASTM C615/C615M - Standard Specification for Granite Dimension Stone
questions.n: ASTM C615/C615M covers granite dimension stone.

questions.q: Which stone family is most directly associated with carbonate sedimentary rock?
questions.ref: ASTM C568/C568M - Standard Specification for Limestone Dimension Stone
questions.n: Limestone is a carbonate sedimentary rock and an important dimension-stone family.

questions.q: What is whitetopping?
o: A concrete overlay on old asphalt
An asphalt overlay on new concrete
questions.ref: American Concrete Pavement Association (ACPA), whitetopping and concrete-overlay guidance
questions.n: Whitetopping is a concrete overlay used to rehabilitate an existing asphalt pavement.

questions.q: A porous banded stone formed by precipitation from mineral-rich water is specified for an interior wall. What stone is being described?
questions.ref: Natural Stone Institute, Dimension Stone Design Manual
questions.n: Travertine is a porous, banded form of limestone deposited from mineral-rich water, commonly at springs.

questions.q: Which stone is classed as an igneous rock?
questions.ref: Natural Stone Institute, Dimension Stone Design Manual
questions.n: Granite forms from cooled magma and is an igneous rock widely used as dimension stone.

questions.q: Which of the following is a bituminous paving material?
questions.ref: Asphalt Institute, The Asphalt Handbook / pavement materials terminology
questions.n: Asphalt is a bituminous binder widely used in flexible pavement.

questions.q: Which laboratory standard is used to determine water absorption of ceramic tile?
questions.ref: ASTM C373 - Standard Test Methods for Determination of Water Absorption and Associated Properties by Vacuum Method for Pressed Ceramic Tiles and Glass Tiles and Boil Method for Extruded Ceramic Tiles
questions.n: ASTM C373 provides standardized methods for determining tile water absorption and related properties.

questions.q: Under standard dimension-stone classifications, travertine belongs to which general stone family?
questions.ref: ASTM C568/C568M - Standard Specification for Limestone Dimension Stone
questions.n: Travertine is a form of limestone and is covered within limestone dimension-stone classification.

questions.q: What is the main structural role of mineral aggregate in asphalt pavement?
o: A part that evaporates on curing
questions.ref: Asphalt Institute, The Asphalt Handbook / pavement materials terminology
questions.n: The aggregate structure carries and distributes much of the load while asphalt binder binds and waterproofs the mixture.

questions.q: Which paving material is the classic example of a flexible pavement surface?
questions.ref: Asphalt Institute, The Asphalt Handbook / pavement materials terminology
questions.n: Flexible pavements typically use asphalt-bound surface courses over granular or stabilized layers.

questions.q: Which standard specifically covers marble dimension stone?
questions.ref: ASTM C503/C503M - Standard Specification for Marble Dimension Stone
questions.n: ASTM C503/C503M covers marble dimension stone.

questions.q: Which stone family is most directly associated with a metamorphosed carbonate rock?
questions.ref: ASTM C503/C503M - Standard Specification for Marble Dimension Stone
questions.n: Marble forms through metamorphism of limestone or dolostone.

questions.q: What is the existing substrate beneath a whitetopping overlay usually made of?
questions.ref: American Concrete Pavement Association (ACPA), whitetopping and concrete-overlay guidance
questions.n: Whitetopping specifically refers to concrete placed over existing asphalt or flexible pavement.

questions.q: What property is measured to classify ceramic tile by how much water it absorbs?
questions.ref: ANSI A137.1 - American National Standard Specifications for Ceramic Tile
questions.n: Ceramic tile classification commonly uses percentage water absorption as a key property.

questions.q: Which common dimension stone is primarily sedimentary?
questions.ref: ASTM C568/C568M - Standard Specification for Limestone Dimension Stone
questions.n: Limestone is a sedimentary rock composed largely of calcium carbonate minerals.

questions.q: Which material is not bituminous?
questions.ref: Cyril M. Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction - stone, tile and paving terminology
questions.n: Bentonite is an expansive clay mineral material, not a bituminous binder.

questions.q: Why is low water absorption important for tile used in wet or exterior conditions?
o: It removes the need for joints
questions.ref: Tile Council of North America (TCNA) Handbook and ceramic tile terminology
questions.n: Lower absorption generally improves resistance to moisture-related deterioration and is an important tile-selection property.

questions.q: Which ASTM terminology standard specifically provides terms used for dimension stone?
questions.ref: ASTM C119 - Standard Terminology Relating to Dimension Stone
questions.n: ASTM C119 is the terminology standard for dimension-stone materials and related terms.
